hindsight_snapshot_fixture_diagnosis.reported_failure: verify-hindsight-recall-snapshot.ts reaches `assert.ok(sourcePrompt.join("\n").includes("BEFORE CLEAR"), "fixture must publish source MM")` and fails after Main adapted the 18.3.3 branch to cfgMemoryBackend.set / cfgHindsightApiUrl.set.
hindsight_snapshot_fixture_diagnosis.verdict: FIXTURE timing, not a 0034 product bug. The 0034 candidate does not touch SessionMemory's listener/apply path or the Settings registry; the state replacement is a direct consequence of writing memory settings on a LIVE session right before the fixture installs its own state.
mechanism: SessionMemory registers a settings listener in its constructor when memory is enabled and an agentDir is present: `value.listen(host, () => this.#observeSettings())` (pi-coding-agent/src/session/session-memory.ts).
`cfgMemoryBackend.set(session.settings, "hindsight")` fires that listener synchronously (Settings.writeValue -> fireIfChanged -> onEffectiveChange).

`#observeSettings()` -> `#applySettingsChange(["memory.backend"])` -> `await this.applyMemoryBackend()` -> `#applyMemoryBackend()`: `await #disposeMemoryBackendState(...)` calls `setHindsightSessionState(undefined)` + `hindsight.dispose()`, then `backend.start(...)` -> `installPrimaryState` installs a FRESH HindsightSessionState and finally `await this.#host.refreshBaseSystemPrompt()`.

The fixture then constructs its own HindsightSessionState, calls `session.setHindsightSessionState(state)`, sets `state.mentalModelsSnippet = "BEFORE CLEAR"` and `await session.refreshBaseSystemPrompt()`. That await yields, so the already-enqueued backend apply completes and REPLACES the fixture state with the fresh one (snippet undefined), leaving no <mental_models> block in the rebuilt prompt.
hindsight_snapshot_fixture_diagnosis.why_it_passed_on_18_2_10: the old fixture used the string-keyed `session.settings.set("memory.backend", ...)`; on 18.2.10 that write did not drive the same live backend apply before the fixture's await, so the fixture state survived. The typed-handle write on 18.3.3 does.
hindsight_snapshot_fixture_diagnosis.exact_fixture_correction: in the 18.3.3 branch of verify-hindsight-recall-snapshot.ts (around lines 445-453), drain the backend apply before the fixture installs its state: after `cfgMemoryBackend.set(...)` and `cfgHindsightApiUrl.set(...)` add `await session.applyMemoryBackend().catch(() => {});`
hindsight_snapshot_fixture_diagnosis.why_applyMemoryBackend_not_settle: `AgentSession.applyMemoryBackend()` (agent-session.ts:5990) returns the coalesced `#memoryBackendTransition` promise, so awaiting it guarantees the pending apply has fully run (even if it rejected: `#applyMemoryBackend`'s catch rethrows, and `.catch(() => {})` keeps the fixture going; after a failed apply the memory state is simply unset and the fixture installs its own state right after). `settleMemoryBackend()` awaits the raw `#settingsChanges` promises, which can reject and abort the drain early, leaving the apply still in flight.
hindsight_snapshot_fixture_diagnosis.no_product_change_needed: with the drain in place the fixture's own state is the primary state when it calls refreshBaseSystemPrompt, so `HindsightSessionMemory.buildDeveloperInstructions` joins its `mentalModelsSnippet` and the assert holds. My 0034 load lifecycle already guards publication with `generation !== this.#mentalModelsLoadGeneration`, so a replaced/disposed state cannot publish a stale snapshot.
